q: Which term describes the measure of the amount of Luminous flux per unit area, quantifying how much light falls onto a surface?
n: Illuminance is luminous flux per unit area falling on a surface, in lux (lm/m²). Source: IES Lighting Handbook, 10th ed., Ch. 2.

q: Which term describes the measure of electromagnetic energy emitted, reflected, transmitted, or received by a surface per unit area per unit solid angle, encompassing both visible and non-visible wavelengths?
n: Radiance is radiant (electromagnetic) power per unit area per unit solid angle, visible or not. Luminance is its visually weighted counterpart. Source: IES Lighting Handbook, 10th ed., Ch. 2.

q: Which term describes the measure of the brightness of a surface as perceived by the human eye, quantifying the amount of visible light emitted or reflected from a surface in a given direction?
n: Luminance (cd/m²) is the perceived brightness of a surface: visible light emitted or reflected in a given direction. Source: IES Lighting Handbook, 10th ed., Ch. 2.

q: Which term describes the total amount of visible light energy emitted by a source per unit time, measured in lumens, regardless of direction or surface area?
n: Luminous flux is the total visible light a source emits per unit time, in lumens, regardless of direction. Source: IES Lighting Handbook, 10th ed., Ch. 2.

q: What is a good general lighting color for office spaces?
n: Cool white (about 4000 K) is the usual general lighting for offices. It is neutral and alert without the blue cast of daylight lamps. Source: IES Lighting Handbook, 10th ed. (CCT recommendations for offices); IES RP-1 (Office Lighting).

q: Warm white
n: Warm white lamps are about 2700–3500 K. Source: IES Lighting Handbook, 10th ed., Ch. 4 (Correlated Color Temperature).

q: Daylight
n: 'Daylight' lamps have a correlated color temperature of about 5,500–6,500 K. Their cool, bluish-white light imitates natural daylight. Source: IES Lighting Handbook, 10th ed., Ch. 4 (CCT).

q: Cool white
n: 'Cool white' lamps have a correlated color temperature of about 4,000–5,000 K. That is whiter than warm white (about 2,700–3,000 K) but less bluish than daylight lamps. Source: IES Lighting Handbook, 10th ed., Ch. 4 (CCT).

q: Which light is suitable for living rooms and bedrooms?
n: Warm white (2700–3500 K) gives a cozy, relaxing light suited to living rooms and bedrooms. Source: IES Lighting Handbook, 10th ed. (residential lighting).

q: Which type of lighting generates diffuse, uniformly scattered light that does not create harsh shadows, making it ideal for general illumination by reflecting off ceilings or walls?
n: Indirect lighting bounces off ceilings or walls, giving diffuse, even light without harsh shadows. Source: IES Lighting Handbook, 10th ed. (luminaire distribution types).

q: Which type of lighting delivers illumination straight from the fixture to the target surface without reflection or diffusion, producing sharp shadows and high contrast, and is commonly used in downlights, floodlights, and pendant fixtures regardless of purpose?
n: Direct lighting sends light straight from the fixture to the surface, giving sharp shadows and high contrast (downlights, floodlights, pendants). Source: IES Lighting Handbook, 10th ed. (luminaire distribution types).

q: Which type of lighting is designed to provide focused illumination for specific activities such as reading, cooking, or working, and is typically brighter and more localized than general lighting?
n: Task lighting is brighter, localized light for specific activities such as reading, cooking or working. Source: IES Lighting Handbook, 10th ed. (layers of light).

q: Which type of lighting is used to highlight specific architectural features, art works, or decorative elements by creating visual emphasis and contrast through focused illumination?
n: Accent lighting highlights architectural features, artwork or decor through focused emphasis and contrast. Source: IES Lighting Handbook, 10th ed. (layers of light).

q: This button is used to request an elevator and is typically mounted 42 inches above the finished floor.
n: The hall call button requests an elevator and is typically centered about 42 in. (1,067 mm) above the floor. Source: ASME A17.1 / ADA Standards, Sec. 407.2.1.1.

q: A standard elevator has two.(2) separate door systems. What do you call the interior door which travels up and down along with the elevator and opens and closes automatically when the elevator arrives at a floor?
n: The car (cab) door travels with the elevator and opens automatically at each floor. Source: ASME A17.1 (car doors); Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook.

q: Which component of an elevator is responsible for sealing the interior of an elevator and moves with it as it travels between floors?
n: The cab door closes off the car interior and moves with the car between floors. Source: ASME A17.1; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook.

q: Elevators shall be provided with controls to reduce the energy demands. To meet this requirement, elevator lighting should switch off how many minutes after it has been inactive?
n: Elevator lighting must switch off after the elevator has been inactive for at most five minutes. Source: Philippine Green Building Code (2015), Sec. 10.6.5.

q: The following are elevator suppliers except?
n: Hyundai, Hitachi and Mitsubishi all make elevators. Meiji is not an elevator supplier. Source: Manufacturer listings (Hyundai Elevator, Hitachi Building Systems, Mitsubishi Electric).

q: Which device designed for intermittent operation, commonly found in restaurants, hospitals, and multi-storey buildings, functions as a vertical transport system, allowing small and lightweight goods to be transferred between floors, but does not accommodate human passengers?
n: A dumbwaiter is a small lift for goods only, not passengers, used in restaurants, hospitals and multi-storey buildings. Source: ASME A17.1, Part 7 (Dumbwaiters).

q: Escalators and moving ramps shall be fitted with controls to automatically reduce to a slower speed when no activity has been detected for a maximum period of?
n: Escalators and moving ramps must slow down automatically when no activity is detected for at most 1½ minutes. Source: Philippine Green Building Code (2015), Sec. 10.6.5.

q: Under the amended BP 344 IRR, what is the minimum clear door opening required for an accessible elevator car?
n: Accessible elevator cars need a clear door opening of at least 900 mm. Source: Amended IRR of BP 344 (2024), Appendix C, Accessible Elevators.

q: What is the primary purpose of providing handrails inside an accessible elevator car, as required by BP 344 and relevant Philippine codes?
o: To provide a mounting surface for signage and emergency instructions
To prevent the elevator doors from closing too quickly during operation
To offer stability and support for passengers during elevator movement
As a decorative element that enhances the interior finish of the elevator
n: Handrails in an accessible car give passengers stability and support while the car moves. Source: Amended IRR of BP 344 (2024), Appendix C, Item 8.6.

q: A part of the air conditioning system wherein the refrigerant absorbs surrounding heat and where the cold air comes from. It is near the air handler, where the blower fan helps spread newly cooled air. It is made from copper or aluminum as these metals easily conduct heat.
n: In the evaporator coil the refrigerant absorbs room heat, producing the cold air that the blower spreads. It is made of copper or aluminum for good heat transfer. Source: ASHRAE Handbook—HVAC Systems and Equipment; Stein & Reynolds, Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings.

q: A part of an air conditioning system, it squeezes the refrigerant which makes its temperature significantly above the surrounding atmosphere.
n: The compressor squeezes refrigerant vapor, raising its pressure and temperature well above the surroundings. Source: ASHRAE Handbook—HVAC Systems and Equipment; Stein & Reynolds, MEEB.

q: A part of the air conditioning system, it receives the hot and pressurized gas. It is here that the gas is transformed into a high-pressure cool liquid.
n: The condenser receives hot, high-pressure gas from the compressor and rejects heat, turning it into a high-pressure liquid. Source: ASHRAE Handbook—HVAC Systems and Equipment; Stein & Reynolds, MEEB.

q: In a vapor-compression air-conditioning system, which component is commonly regarded as the "heart" of the system because it creates the pressure differential necessary to circulate refrigerant throughout the entire refrigeration cycle?
n: The compressor is the "heart" of the cycle. It creates the pressure difference that circulates the refrigerant. Source: ASHRAE Handbook—HVAC Systems and Equipment.

q: A window-type air-conditioning unit contains both the heat-absorbing and heat-rejecting sections within a single cabinet. Which component is intentionally positioned toward the exterior side of the unit to facilitate the transfer of unwanted heat to the surrounding atmosphere?
n: In a window unit, the condenser coil faces outside so heat is rejected outdoors. Source: Stein & Reynolds, MEEB (unitary equipment).

q: In a split-type. air conditioning system, what do you call the component that contains the compressor, condenser coil, and fan, and is responsible for rejecting heat to the atmosphere?
n: The outdoor unit (condensing unit) holds the compressor, condenser coil and fan, and rejects heat outdoors. Source: ASHRAE Handbook—HVAC Systems and Equipment (split systems).

q: A proposed school building includes multiple lecture halls where wall areas are heavily utilized for marker boards, projection screens, storage systems, and instructional displays. Due to these space constraints, the designer is considering air-conditioning solutions commonly recommended for tight spaces while still achieving efficient and uniform cooling throughout the room. Which type of split-type air-conditioning system is generally the most appropriate for this application?
n: Ceiling cassette units free the walls and distribute air four ways for even cooling, which suits lecture halls with busy walls. Source: ASHRAE Handbook—HVAC Systems and Equipment (ductless split systems).

q: A chilled-water air-conditioning system is designed so that classrooms can be conditioned independently without requiring each room to be connected directly to a large central air-distribution unit. Which equipment would most likely be installed within or adjacent to each classroom to accomplish this objective?
n: Fan coil units in or next to each room take chilled water and condition the room independently, without a central air handler for every space. Source: ASHRAE Handbook—HVAC Systems and Equipment (Fan-Coil Units).

q: In a split-type air conditioning system, which component serves as the primary conduit for refrigerant flow between the indoor and outdoor units. enabling heat transfer across the refrigeration cycle?
n: Insulated copper tubing (the line set) carries refrigerant between the indoor and outdoor units. Source: ASHRAE Handbook—HVAC Systems and Equipment (split systems).

q: A part of the air conditioning system, it regulates the flow of refrigerant for optimal performance.
n: The expansion valve meters refrigerant into the evaporator for optimum performance. Source: ASHRAE Handbook—HVAC Systems and Equipment (refrigerant flow controls).

q: What is the function of an HVAC (airflow) damper?
o: Removes unwanted air from inside to outside of the building
Brings air conditioning to any part of the building
Stops or regulates the flow of air in the building
Serves as a commercial and industrial grade exhaust duct
n: A damper is a plate or blade assembly in a duct that stops or regulates the flow of air. It is used for balancing, zoning, and fire/smoke control. Source: Stein & Reynolds, Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (HVAC – Air Distribution); ASHRAE Handbook – Fundamentals.

q: A roof-mounted exhaust vent whose fan is powered by its own built-in photovoltaic panel, used to draw hot air out of the attic, is called a
n: A solar roof vent is a roof-mounted exhaust fan powered by its own photovoltaic panel. It draws hot air out of the attic without using grid power. Source: Stein & Reynolds, Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (Attic Ventilation); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 7.

q: A ceiling-mounted supply outlet that spreads conditioned air into a room in a diffused pattern is called a/an
n: An air diffuser is the supply-air outlet, usually round or square on the ceiling, that spreads conditioned air into the room in a diffused pattern. Source: Stein & Reynolds, Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (Air Distribution Devices); ASHRAE Handbook – Fundamentals.

q: Which of the following is the most effective and specialized solution for reducing noise transmission in air ducts?
o: Adding insulation around ducts to absorb sound and reduce vibrations
Increasing duct diameter to lower air velocity
Using a sound attenuator to specifically dampen noise
Installing airflow dampers to regulate pressure changes
n: Sound attenuators (duct silencers) are built specifically to reduce noise traveling through ducts. Source: ASHRAE Handbook—HVAC Applications, Ch. 49 (Noise and Vibration Control).

q: Which of the following is the most versatile component in an HVAC system, capable of regulating airflow, controlling pressure. contributing to noise control, and preventing the spread of fire and smoke?
n: Dampers regulate airflow and pressure, help control noise, and (as fire/smoke dampers) stop fire and smoke spreading. That makes them the most versatile component here. Source: ASHRAE Handbook—HVAC Systems and Equipment; NFPA 90A.

q: Which HVAC component is primarily used to regulate or restrict airflow within a duct distribution system'?
n: A damper regulates or restricts airflow in a duct. Source: ASHRAE Handbook—HVAC Systems and Equipment.

q: Which type of metal sheet, when wrapped in insulation and placed inside a solid duct section of an HVAC system, is most effective at reducing airborne noise by allowing sound waves to pass through and be absorbed'?
n: Perforated metal liners backed by insulation let sound pass through and be absorbed, reducing duct noise. Source: ASHRAE Handbook—HVAC Applications, Ch. 49.

q: Which of the following best describes Air Changes Per Hour (ACH) in a ventilation system?
o: The frequency at which an HVAC system filters air
The number of times an air purifier processes indoor air following ASHRAE standards
The rate at which indoor air is replaced by fresh air within a space
The number of times an air conditioner cycles per hour
n: Air changes per hour (ACH) is how many times per hour the room air is replaced by fresh air. Source: ASHRAE Standard 62.1; ASHRAE Fundamentals, Ch. 16.

q: What does the acronym PVC stand for in construction and material science
n: PVC stands for polyvinyl chloride, the rigid thermoplastic widely used for drainage, waste and vent piping and for electrical conduit. Source: ASTM D1784 (PVC compounds).

q: Cheapest electrical conduit
n: PVC conduit is the cheapest of RMC, EMT, IMC and PVC. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (PEC 2017), Art. 3.52; local material price lists.

q: Which conduit type is both flexible and non-metallic, making it suitable for underground electrical installations?
n: HDPE conduit is flexible and non-metallic, and comes in long coils for underground runs. PVC is rigid. EMT and RMC are metallic. Source: PEC 2017, Art. 3.53 (HDPE Conduit).
